title: Schrock et al. v. Philadelphia Presbytery
disposition_detail: Complaint sustained on the issue whether Philadelphia Presbytery failed to judge and record TE Larry Smith’s views on the continuation of prophecy and tongues beyond the apostolic era under BCO 13-6, 21-4e-f, and RAO 16-3.e.5; matter remanded for Presbytery to receive a written statement in Smith’s own words and categorically judge it. The SJC did not hold Smith’s views erroneous, did not reverse his transfer, and noted future action could only arise from changed views, a BCO 31-2 investigation, or charges. Dissents would have denied the complaint.
first_summary: The SJC sustained a complaint against Philadelphia Presbytery, holding it erred in approving TE Larry Smith’s transfer exam without judging and recording his views on the continuation of prophecy and tongues. It remanded for Presbytery to obtain and categorically judge Smith’s stated difference.
summary: The SJC sustained a complaint against Philadelphia Presbytery for failing to judge and record TE Larry Smith’s stated difference over the continuation of prophecy and tongues beyond the apostolic era. The record showed Presbytery approved Smith’s transfer exam and defeated a motion to find his view out of accord, but it did not categorize that view in Smith’s own words. The SJC remanded for a written statement and Presbytery’s categorical judgment, without undoing Smith’s transfer or deciding whether his view was erroneous.

sources.supports: Case identity, parties, procedural history, issue, judgment sustaining complaint and remanding.
Adopted reasoning: RAO 16-3.e.5 categorization duty, insufficient record, remand instructions, no effect on transfer, and SJC vote 14-5-2.
Separate dissenting opinions by Donahoe et al. and Nusbaum, not adopted; they argued denial and challenged the RAO/stated-difference analysis.

evidence_notes.identity_and_adoption: Case 2019-02, TE Daniel Schrock et al. v. Philadelphia Presbytery; SJC decision on complaint dated Oct. 18, 2019, reported in 48th GA (2021), p. 668. The Panel’s proposed decision was written by TE Greco; the SJC revised the reasoning and approved by 14-5-2, with three absent (lines 13–15, 93).
evidence_notes.dispute: Complainants challenged Presbytery’s approval of TE Larry Smith’s transfer exam and its failure to judge/record the nature of his stated difference on the continuation of prophecy and tongues beyond the apostolic era under BCO 13-6, 21-4e-f, and RAO 16-3.e.5. Presbytery denied; complainants carried the complaint to the General Assembly (lines 19–39, 45–47).
evidence_notes.outcomes_and_reasons: The SJC answered yes, sustained the complaint, and remanded. It reasoned that Presbytery did not record or categorize Smith’s view in his own words and took no specific action on that stated difference; the record was unclear and insufficient. Smith’s transfer was unaffected, and future action could only arise from changed views, a BCO 31-2 investigation, or charges (lines 49–51, 65–79, 91).
evidence_notes.qualifications: The majority did not find Smith’s view out of accord; it required only a further written statement and categorical judgment. Dissents by Donahoe, Cannata, Lucas, Terrell, and by Nusbaum argued the complaint should have been denied; they are not adopted (lines 97–105, 448–488).
evidence_notes.incorporated_decisions: None material. The majority does not incorporate another decision. The dissent discusses Lewis v. Mississippi Valley and prior RPR citations; those are not adopted authority for the judgment (lines 188–198, 214–218).
